title: Dawn phenomenon — hybrid HGP + circadian ISF model (Bolli & Gerich 1984 / simulator extension)

flows.label: scales kb1, kb2, kb3 each tick

caption.scope: Simulator implementation of the dawn phenomenon (Bolli & Gerich, N Engl J Med 310:746-750, 1984), split into two coupled mechanisms. Mechanism 1 — hepatic glucose output: a sine-arc circadianCortisol signal (peak 08:00, amplitude 0.15) is added to stressMultiplier, raising EGP = EGP₀ · max(0, stressMultiplier − x3). Mechanism 2 — peripheral insulin sensitivity: circadianISF varies from 0.70 (08:00) to 1.20 (evening) and rescales kb1/kb2/kb3, so the same plasma insulin produces less peripheral effect at dawn. The amplitude baseAmp is recalculated at midnight as 0.15 · (1 + 0.12·h_lost) · (1 + 0.30·chronicStress), so poor sleep and residual cortisol amplify the next morning's rise. Combined effect at 08:00: stressMultiplier contribution 1.15 and circadianISF 0.70 yield approximately 64 % more insulin needed than at evening baseline. This is a simulator extension; the original Bolli/Gerich observation has been extended with a circadian ISF component informed by Schmidt et al. (2014).

variables.definition: time of day in 24-hour clock (00–24 h), drives circadian phase for both mechanisms
hours of sleep lost relative to target (clamped 0–4 h); read from player input, resets at 07:00
residual cortisol carry-over from previous day (t½ ≈ 12 h); updated each midnight
circadian cortisol signal — symmetric sine arc, rises 04:00, peaks 08:00, falls 12:00; amplitude set by baseAmp
circadian insulin sensitivity factor — cosine interpolation: 1.20 (00–04), 0.70 (08:00), 1.00 (14:00), 1.20 (19–24)
combined stress term (≥ 1) fed into EGP equation; includes glycogenBaseline, gngBaseline, acute, chronic, dawn, and protein-glucagon components
net ISF modifier = baseISF · circadianISF · vasodilatation · postExBoost / (insulinResist · ffaResist)
hepatic endogenous glucose production; stress raises EGP, x3 (insulin action) suppresses it
build-up rate constants for insulin effect compartments x1 (transport), x2 (disposal), x3 (EGP suppression); all scaled each tick by currentISF
sleep deficit contribution to dawn amplitude: +12 percentage points per hour of lost sleep
chronic stress contribution to dawn amplitude: +30 percentage points per unit of chronicStress
clock-to-circadianCortisol mapping: active window 04:00–12:00, symmetric sine shape, peak at 08:00
clock-to-circadianISF mapping: cosine interpolation through four control points across 24 h
hepatic glucose output rate entering plasma pool Q1 (mmol/min)
ISF-scaled build-up rates delivered to x1, x2, x3 each simulation tick
